answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a wander, before it can post or attest. A single lagoon checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 450 aliases therefore burns 206 bonds held for 10 days each, plus the ferrous attestations those aliases can never earn. That is 39 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
